prompt.context: The maker of Botox is considering expanding to the migraine market and has already begun clinical trials in this arena. The product is scheduled to launch in 2014.
prompt.question: What are your estimates of the size of the migraine market in both units sold and revenue? If the market is attractive, do you have any recommendations regarding how to launch the product?

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of the product?
clarifying_info.a: The drug will be priced at $200 per injection.

clarifying_info.q: How often is the injection administered?
clarifying_info.a: The injection is given every 2 months.
This drug will be produced worldwide, so use world population of approximately 6-7 billion.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of the population suffers from migraines?
clarifying_info.a: A reasonable estimate is 20% of the population suffers from chronic headaches/migraines.

clarifying_info.q: What share of migraine sufferers have severe migraines and would use prescription products?
clarifying_info.a: Assume about 50% of chronic migraine sufferers experience severe migraines and are willing to purchase prescription products.

clarifying_info.q: What market share can we expect?
clarifying_info.a: Due to the absence of side effects and added skin care benefits, assume 40% of the overall market in 5 years. If generic competition is raised, assume 20%.
Imitrex, the market leader in traditional prescription migraine treatments, lost patent protection last year. Candidate should discuss the possibility of aggressive entry of generic competition.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of migraine sufferers would try this medicine?
clarifying_info.a: Assume at least 10% of migraine sufferers are willing to try such a medicine.

clarifying_info.q: What are the product's attributes vs. competition?
clarifying_info.a: It offers similar efficacy compared to the market-leading option but without any side effects. When taken for migraines it also has some added skin care benefits.

framework: Market sizing: Estimate the total addressable market for prescription migraine treatments (units and revenue) using a population-based approach
Product assessment: Evaluate the product's competitive positioning (no side effects, skin care benefits, pricing vs. alternatives)
Competitive landscape: Assess impact of generic competition following Imitrex patent expiration
Market attractiveness: Determine if projected revenue justifies investment
Launch strategy: Brand naming decision (existing Botox brand vs. new brand), pricing, and go-to-market approach
Risks and mitigations: Cannibalization, pricing backlash, generic entry

questions.prompt: Calculate the total market size in number of patients (units) and annual revenue for the prescription migraine market worldwide.
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through a clear population funnel: world population → % with chronic migraines → % with severe migraines (prescription-eligible). Then layer in price and injection frequency to get revenue. Should arrive at ~600M patients and ~$720B annual market.

math.setup: World population × % chronic migraine sufferers × % severe (prescription-eligible) = total patients. Annual revenue per patient = price per injection × injections per year. Total market = patients × annual revenue per patient.
steps: Price per injection: $200; injections per year: 12 months / 2 months = 6 injections/year
math.answer: Total market: 600M patients, $720B annually. Botox addressable market: $144B–$288B depending on generic competition.

questions.prompt: Given the market size, is this an attractive market to enter?
questions.guidance: Candidate should conclude that $144B–$288B in addressable revenue is very large and makes this market highly attractive, assuming marginal costs are low (typical for drugs) and that the profit margin is substantial. Key takeaway: the market is large enough to consider investment.

questions.prompt: How should Botox launch this product — under the existing Botox brand name or a new brand?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will weigh both sides. New brand: allows differentiation between cosmetic and migraine use cases, enables cleaner advertising to patients and physicians, and reduces backlash from differential pricing between the two indications. Existing brand: leverages the strong Botox brand reputation already built.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks and considerations around launching this product?

categories.name: Pricing & Cannibalization
ideas: Same drug sold for two different indications could trigger public outcry over price discrepancy between migraine and cosmetic versions
Patients may substitute the migraine form for the cosmetic form, cannibalizing existing Botox cosmetic sales

categories.name: Branding
ideas: Launching under a new brand name can differentiate use cases and reduce pricing backlash
Retaining the Botox name brings existing brand recognition and trust
New brand requires additional marketing investment to build awareness

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Imitrex lost patent protection, so aggressive generic entry could depress pricing and share
40% market share assumption may be optimistic if generics proliferate quickly
Need to monitor competitive response from generic manufacturers

categories.name: Regulatory & Clinical
ideas: Clinical trials already underway; regulatory approval timeline and outcomes are key risks
Any adverse findings in trials could delay or prevent launch

categories.name: Market Access
ideas: Physician education needed given new indication for a known cosmetic drug
Payer (insurance) coverage for migraine indication vs. cosmetic use has different dynamics
Patient willingness to accept injectable treatment for migraines vs. oral options

recommendation: The prescription migraine market is very large ($720B annually, ~600M patients) with strong profit potential given the drug's low marginal cost profile
Recommend proceeding with the launch under a new brand name to differentiate from the cosmetic Botox product, avoid pricing backlash, and enable cleaner physician and patient marketing
risks: Launching under the Botox name risks public outcry over pricing discrepancy and could cannibalize cosmetic Botox sales
Generic competition following Imitrex patent expiration could reduce market share to the lower end of the range (20%, ~$144B)
next_steps: Confirm clinical trial outcomes and regulatory pathway for migraine indication
Develop new brand identity and marketing strategy targeting neurologists and migraine patients
Model cannibalization risk quantitatively against incremental revenue from migraine indication
Conduct competitive analysis on generic Imitrex entrants to stress-test market share assumptions
